Uniform differentiation is not proved.
notes.detailedSummary: The argument reconstructs the supplied root and norm constructions without importing the embedded round55 notes. The rational energy bridge uses normal full section rings, genuine line-bundle frames, CLD fiber currents with one-unit Gauss mass, the degree-d Veronese cover, and BHJ model/DH energy compatibility. A homogeneous rank-d free Rees submodule and a common homogeneous denominator yield filtered injections and O(m^n) signed cutoff errors. Rational index clearing uses valuation dilation rather than multiplication of a potential. Real weights and irrational Reeb fields pass through signed-mean and genuine local-uniform CLD energy continuity. These are unverified draft mathematical claims; they do not complete the original target.
notes.text:
Work on a normal good affine cone R of dimension n>=1 over any algebraically closed trivially valued characteristic-zero field. The premises are the ten exact public bodies supplied in the input, particularly Wu2406.13684v1, BJ1801.08229v4, CLD1204.6277v2, BHJ1504.06568v3 and BE1805.01016v3. No embedded generated note is trusted.

Choose homogeneous algebra generators h_i of weights beta_i, write d_theta(alpha)=<theta,alpha>, and use the compact carrier K={v=q(v):min_i v(h_i)=0}. The actual torified action is (v+t eta)(sum f_alpha)=min_alpha(v(f_alpha)+t d_eta(alpha)). The reference rho_theta=max_i[-v(h_i)/d_theta(beta_i)] gives an orbit section s_theta(v)=v+rho_theta(v)theta in K. Every theta-equivariant potential satisfies u(v)=u(s_theta(v))+rho_theta(v). A primary FS list has some member of value zero at every point of K: otherwise an expression of a zero-valued h_i^r in that primary ideal would have positive value. Thus zero-weight primary references agree.

Every supported nonzero weight is a nonnegative integer combination of the beta_i. Therefore c=min_i d_eta(beta_i)/d_xi(beta_i) and C=max_i of those ratios bound all supported degree ratios. The inequalities u(v)-Ct<=u(v+t eta)<=u(v)-ct for t>=0 pass from FS through local uniform and decreasing completions. At finite points the orbit has a unique zero; at a minus-infinite point the whole orbit is minus infinity. Define R_xi,eta u by that zero parameter, with value minus infinity in the latter case. Its FS formula is exactly max_j[(lambda_j-v(f_j))/d_eta(alpha_j)], proving presentation independence.

Uniform errors move roots by at most their size divided by c. For decreasing nets, bracket each finite root by two fixed orbit points; at a minus-infinite limit use v-M eta for arbitrary M. These arguments prove actual H/CPSH/PSH membership and preservation of defining decreasing nets. Equal zero sets give inverse and cocycle. Sup_K u=u(v_triv) is finite, and normalized roots remain normalized. The raw map does not descend modulo constants: on k[x,y], xi=(1,1), eta=(1,2), R(rho_xi+2)-rho_eta takes values 2 and 1 at v_triv and (3,0). Full-pointwise continuity does not imply continuity in the weaker quasimonomial or strong topology.

For homogeneous algebra generators g_i with signed assigned weights lambda_i, define F^a R_alpha as the span of monomials of weight alpha having assigned weight at least a, and chi(f) as its greatest filtration index. There are finitely many eligible monomials per weight space. This quotient filtration retains relations, is multiplicative, and is linearly bounded by the smallest and largest generator weight/degree ratios. Replacing lambda_i by chi(g_i) preserves the filtration: increasing assigned weights gives one inclusion, and multiplicativity gives the reverse. Its exact potential is sup_f(chi(f)-v(f))/d_theta(f)=max_i(lambda_i-v(g_i))/d_theta(g_i). The upper bound uses an expression attaining chi(f), the valuation inequality and a weighted average of generator expressions; the lower bound uses each g_i. Infinite evaluations cause no exception. Appending sufficiently negative algebra generators to a primary list changes no potential on a compact Reeb slice or, by equivariance, anywhere.

For rational eta=s eta_e use the effective integer grading of gcd one. Choose d sufficiently divisible that A=R^(d) and the index-cleared Rees Veronese are generated in new degree one. Generation follows by extracting generator powers of a common degree d0, bounding residual monomial degrees, and choosing d divisible by d0 above that bound. A=R^(mu_d) is normal, finite in R, and the faithful character decomposition gives fraction-field degree d. Every residue occurs because the positive degree semigroup has gcd one. V=Proj R is normal. The localizations A[a^-1]=A[a^-1]_0[a,a^-1] identify the punctured standard cone with the genuine L_d^-1 torsor. For n>=2, Hartogs across the vertex gives A_l=H^0(V,lL_d). For n=1 the effective normal good ring is k[z] and V is a point.

Restriction of the norm to A has the same potential after scaling: the full supremum gives one inequality and powers of each generator lying in A give the other. For the actual degree-d map p:Spec R->Spec A, p*Phi=sd u_eta and p*rho_d=sd rho_eta, including positive parts.

In a genuine L_d frame, Phi=log|t|+h and rho=log|t|+h0, with t of fiber degree one. Under e_j=a_ij e_i, t_j=a_ij t_i and h0,j=h0,i-log|a_ij|. Tensor the projective FS bundles by their actual section exponents to meet CLD's integer-paralinear hypothesis; CLD12.5.2 permits real constants. CLD18.6.1 on the flat, separated, equidimensional, boundaryless torsor identifies the horizontal top current with sum_v a_v delta_(Y_v), where sum a_v delta_v is the actual projective mixed curvature measure. On its H(v)-fiber, CLD18.6.2 gives ddc max(log|t|+h0(v),0) one unit Dirac mass at radius exp(-h0(v)). Smooth convex approximation and CLD8.7.2 give, for every local smooth test q, integral q T ddc rho^+=sum_v a_v q(i(v)). Partitions of unity and CLD6.2.6 give all continuous local tests. Frame changes preserve i(v). These applications include singular bases. Uniform FS limits use weighted-current continuity. A section of mL cannot replace a degree-one frame without the radial 1/m.

CLD13.3.7 gives calibrated finite-map degree d because the target is reduced. CLD16.1.5 supplies one pushforward factor d after n curvature/radial factors 1/(sd). Consequently the genuine raw mass is V_eta=s^(-n)d^(1-n)(L_d^(n-1)), the transverse class is omega_eta=L_d/(sd), and normalized cone energy is E_Ld/(sd). Homogeneous values in R are recovered from their dth powers in A; finite-map surjectivity supplies the unique torified lift. Normalized cone and projective measures agree under this carrier identification.

For integral indices, the finitely generated Rees filtration of the full section ring gives an ample test configuration by BHJ2.15, with metric equal to the exact FS supremum. Graph normalization preserves this metric, and BHJ3.14 preserves DH because V is reduced. BHJ5.9 identifies the degree-wise spectral limit with DH; linear bounds permit signed first moments. BHJ3.12(iii), 7.2--7.4 and 6.7 identify its mean with genuine normalized projective energy. Model probability coefficients are b_E times mixed intersections divided by (L_d^(n-1)); a vertical coefficient r_E evaluates to r_E/b_E. There is no second division by volume. BE8.18 and CLD18.4.7 supply actual model/curvature compatibility. For rational indices, the metric of b chi is b phi(v/b), not b phi(v). BJ7.2/7.7 and BHJ6.3/6.13 give energy scaling by b under this valuation-dilation action. Dividing mean and energy by b returns the rational filtration; line-bundle tensoring is a separate operation.

For the full-ring passage, Gamma is finite over B=Gamma^(d), of fraction rank d. Choose homogeneous elements e_j in all residues giving a free submodule F=sum B e_j. Clear homogeneous fractions of a finite module generating set to obtain one homogeneous nonzero c with c Gamma contained in F. Specializing t=1 yields filtered injections F_(<=m)->R_(<=m) and cR_(<=m)->F_(<=m+a), with fixed degree/index shifts. A filtered injection increasing indices by b has descending spectral weights w_i>=u_i+b. Unmatched dimensions contribute at most their count times the O(m) linear weight bound. Hilbert asymptotics bound dimension errors by O(m^(n-1)), hence signed weight errors by O(m^n). Thus W_R(m)=dW_A(m/d)+O(m^n), accounting for every residue; in dimension one the error is O(m), negligible against mN(m). Summing degree-wise means e gives cumulative mean ne/(n+1). Combined with the genuine radial calibration, this proves E_eta=(n+1)S_chi(eta)/n for rational data.

Real assigned-weight perturbations change each spectral jump by at most epsilon times its degree. The exact own-degree shift is W_shift=W+A D, where D=mN(m)-integral_0^m N(t)dt and D/(mN)->n/(n+1). For nonpositive lists, cutoff inclusions give W_xi(m/c)<=W_eta(m)<=W_xi(m/C). Rational approximation squeezes existence at irrational fields and yields exp(±(2n+1)delta) comparison of negative means, where delta=max_i|log degree-ratio|. The same dimension inclusions prove continuous positive volume at irrational fields. Normalize arbitrary lists using their own degree and a(theta)=max_i lambda_i/d_theta(g_i), apply the nonpositive comparison and perturbation bounds, and add back only a(theta)n/(n+1). CLD8.7.2 with moving radial currents and continuous energy weights proves genuine bounded/local-uniform mixed-MA and energy convergence on K. This passes the identity to all real weights and irrational fields and establishes presentation independence.

These are draft mathematical arguments, not consequences of execution checks. Details are in P13.1-argument.md Sections2--8 and P13.1-paper.tex. notes.summary: Using n1, normalized genuine energies satisfy exp(±(2n+1)delta) comparison and roots preserve actual E1 through raw decreasing nets. A canonical outer energy agrees with existing energy and has explicit bounded-obstacle Reeb continuity. Differentiation remains unproved.
notes.detailedSummary: The signed representation converts cutoff inequalities into genuine energy estimates uniform in potentials and presentations. Because normalizing defining approximants can destroy monotonicity, the proof retains raw decreasing root images and controls their energy differences from normalized images. The continuous-obstacle supremum F and usc outer extension F-downarrow agree with existing CPSH and PSH energies respectively. Bounded-competitor truncation proves Reeb continuity. Residual torification equates torified and unrestricted rational-projective energy suprema, but does not identify either with relative volume.
notes.text:
Use n1's intrinsic roots, genuine signed energy identity, cutoff comparison and bounded CLD continuity. Let delta=max_i|log(d_eta(beta_i)/d_xi(beta_i))| and k=2n+1. For u normalized by u(v_triv)=0,

exp(-k delta)(-E_xi(u)) <= -E_eta(R_xi,eta u) <= exp(k delta)(-E_xi(u)).

On FS this follows from nonpositive assigned weights and E=(n+1)S/n. Uniform FS approximation, root Lipschitzness and genuine energy monotonicity/translation extend it to CPSH. On compact Q, delta<=L_Q||eta-xi||, with L_Q=max_i ||beta_i||_dual/min_(theta in Q)d_theta(beta_i). Constants are independent of potentials, presentations and rational denominators.

Actual PSH energy is the infimum over dominating CPSH. If u_i decreases to u and w>=u is CPSH, the open sets {u_i<w+epsilon} cover compact K; directedness gives u_i<=w+epsilon eventually. Monotonicity/translation followed by infimum over w proves E(u_i)->E(u), including minus infinity. For normalized E1 u, put a_i=u_i(v_triv), decreasing to zero, and v_i=u_i-a_i. The v_i need not decrease. Their energies tend to E(u), and the normalized comparison applies. The root slope bound gives ||R u_i-R v_i||<=|a_i|/c, also bounding the energy difference. The raw roots R u_i decrease to R u and have a finite lower energy bound. Decreasing continuity proves R u in E1 and passes the comparison to it. Applying the inverse gives onto normalized E1 quotients. No strong-topology or unbounded moving-field mixed-MA theorem is claimed.

Define F_eta(g)=sup{E_eta(w):w in CPSH(eta), w|K<=g} for continuous g. The reference plus min g is feasible; all competitors lie below the reference plus max g. Thus min g<=F(g)<=max g, F is monotone, F(g+a)=F(g)+a and |F(g)-F(g')|<=||g-g'||. For an actual CPSH restriction u, feasibility and energy monotonicity give F(u)=E(u).

If ||g||<=M, replace every competitor by max(w,rho_eta-M), preserving CPSH and feasibility and increasing energy. Hence -M<=w|K<=M suffices. Write w=Nw+a, with |a|<=M and -2M<=Nw<=0. The constant-shift root estimate gives ||R(w)-R(Nw)-a||<=M(exp(delta)-1). Combining it with normalized energy comparison bounds the energy transfer error by 2M(exp(k delta)-1)+M(exp(delta)-1). Also ||Rw-w||<=M(exp(delta)-1); subtract this amount to restore feasibility. Taking suprema and reversing the fields proves

|F_eta(g)-F_xi(g)| <= 2M[exp(k delta)-1+exp(delta)-1].

This controls bounded obstacles uniformly; an unbounded pointwise root estimate alone would not control the supremum.

On a rational quotient, eigen-section charts of the naturally linearized L_d define continuous residual torification q_V. The canonical reference is unchanged, and the Gauss section with n1's unique lift identifies K with its image. Splitting each section of a projective FS metric psi into residual weight components, retaining its coefficient, gives an actual globally generating FS metric psi composed with q_V. Ultrametricity gives psi composed with q_V>=psi. Uniform FS approximation gives the CPSH assertion. If g=g composed with q_V and psi<=g, the torified metric is still feasible. Energy monotonicity therefore equates torified and unrestricted projective ENERGY suprema. Obstacle invariance alone would not prove this, and no volume identity follows yet.

For upper-semicontinuous bounded-above h, define F_down(h)=inf{F(g):g continuous, g>=h}. It is monotone, has exact translation and agrees with F on continuous obstacles. For actual PSH u and defining u_i decreasing to u, F_down(u)<=E(u_i). Conversely every continuous g>=u eventually bounds u_i up to epsilon by compactness, giving E(u)<=F(g)+epsilon. Thus F_down(u)=E(u), including minus-infinite energy. The identical compactness argument proves decreasing continuity for arbitrary bounded-above usc nets. Therefore, for E1 u and continuous f,

F_down(u+t f)=lim_i F(u_i+t f), and |F_down(u+t f)-E(u)|<=|t| ||f||.

This is independent of the defining net and constructs an actual extension of existing energy. It does not assert an unproved E(P(u+t f)) equality or establish a derivative. The remaining differentiation gate is n3. Details are in P13.1-argument.md Sections9 and12.

notes.detailedSummary: BGM Lemma3.2 works on geometrically reduced projective schemes over arbitrary complete non-Archimedean fields without an envelope antecedent. Its reductions and restriction/Riemann–Roch proof are audited with the raw factors retained. A common rational-FS lattice of directions on K is dense and admits uniform positive domination in A omega_eta on compact Reeb slices. BE9.15 supplies continuous-psh equality only; its degree-m FS supnorm isometry does not supply signed-mean convergence of the generated higher-degree norms. BJ8.7 explicitly needs an additional approximation theorem; the supplied supporting BJ1805.11160 theorem has standing smoothness and invokes an external lattice result. Thus only relative-volume differentiation is established.
notes.text:
Use n1's rational quotient omega_eta=L_d/(sd) and probability MA, and n2's genuine obstacle supremum and outer extension.

Fix rational xi0. Let D be the rational linear span of differences of rational-weight primary FS functions at xi0 restricted to K, allowing arbitrary positive rational equivariant slopes in intermediate expressions. Products after clearing exponents represent positive sums; maxima concatenate primary lists; reference padding matches slopes. Every element is A0(phi-psi) for positive rational A0 and actual rational FS phi,psi at xi0. The identity max(a-b,c-d)=max(a+d,c+b)-(b+d), allowing the common slope to increase before rescaling, proves lattice closure; negation gives minima. Rational constants are reference translates. Distinct torified points differ on a homogeneous g, and max((lambda-v(g))/d_xi0(g),-M) with primary padding separates them for suitable rational lambda,M, including infinite valuations. Its closure is a real vector lattice separating points and containing constants, hence all C(K).

For f=A0(phi-psi), extend by f_eta(v)=f(v+rho_eta(v)eta). Put r_j(eta)=A0 d_eta(f_j)/d_xi0(f_j) for each branch and choose one rational A exceeding all r_j for both lists and compact Q. Then

a_eta=max_j[A0(lambda_j-v(f_j))/d_xi0(f_j)+(A-r_j(eta))rho_eta],

and its analogous b_eta satisfy a_eta-b_eta=f_eta and have slope A. For rational eta, expand rho_eta over h_l and clear positive rational logarithmic coefficients. Each branch becomes an actual monomial FS expression whose eta/A degree equals its denominator. The product list is primary because away from the vertex some primary f_j and some h_l are nonzero. Thus a_eta,b_eta are actual FS(eta/A). Rational approximants followed by roots back to fixed eta/A converge uniformly on K, proving actual CPSH membership for irrational eta. Their difference on K is exactly the single fixed f. On rational quotients the auxiliary positivity class is A omega_eta.

BGM2004.03847v1 Lemma3.2, LF647--724, assumes geometrically reduced projective X, ample L, continuous psh phi on L, and continuous psh psi1,psi2 on auxiliary ample M. With p=dim X, f=psi1-psi2 and C=(L+M)^p-L^p,

C inf f <= integral f(ddc phi+ddc psi1)^p-vol(L,phi+f,phi) <= C sup f.

There is no envelope assumption. Its proof passes to an algebraically closed nontrivially valued complete extension, uses uniform nef-model approximation and a higher reduced-special-fiber model, perturbs toward ample models, and clears tensor powers. BE1805.01016v3 supplies volume/MA field-extension compatibility. Actual BE PropositionA.15 supplies relatively regular sections under flatness, projectivity, finite presentation and relative ampleness, by prime avoidance on associated fiber points. These restrict regularly to effective vertical divisors by BGM1.2.

Normalize inf f=0, so its vertical divisor E is effective on the reduced special fiber. Restriction sequences give a determinant-volume bound by sum_(j=1)^m h^0(E,(mL+jE)|E), at most m h^0(E,m(L+M1)|E). BGM2.4 gives h^0(E,mN|E)=m^p/p! integral phi_E(ddc phi_N)^p+O(m^(p-1)). Its proof uses Serre vanishing, the degree-p determinant difference and Deligne/curvature compatibility. Dividing by m^(p+1)/p! proves the left bound. Normalize sup f=0, use effective D=-E and sequences for mL-jD to obtain the right bound. Constant shifts move the difference by aC, giving the stated two-sided estimate.

On the rational quotient apply this to epsilon psi1,epsilon psi2, first for rational epsilon by tensor clearing and then by metric continuity. Divide raw volume by V=omega^p. The expanded positive measure V^(-1)(ddc phi+epsilon ddc psi1)^p equals the original probability plus positive terms of total mass (1+epsilon A)^p-1. Bound both the source-estimate error and the added integral by epsilon times that mass times ||f||. For t<0 interchange psi1,psi2. Therefore

|vol(omega,phi+t f,phi)/V-t integral f MA_omega(phi)| <= 2|t|[(1+A|t|)^p-1]||f||
<= 2pA(1+A tau)^(p-1)||f|| t^2, for |t|<=tau and p>=1.

For p=0 the quotient is a point and the remainder is zero. The bound is independent of the potential and rational denominators. It is a RELATIVE-VOLUME estimate.

The unresolved step is the reverse inequality in

sup_(psi continuous psh, psi<=g) E_L(psi)=vol(L,g,h0)/(L^p)

for every continuous obstacle on every normal possibly singular quotient. The <= direction follows from BE Theorem9.15 and monotonicity. That theorem identifies volume with energy only for two continuous psh metrics; Corollary9.16 separately assumes envelopes. BE7.26/7.27 give dominated FS approximants and degree-m supnorm isometry, but not determinant-mean convergence for the quotient norms they generate in all multiples of m.

BJ1801.08229v4 LF4888--4900 explicitly obtains this additional convergence through [Reb21, Theorem5.1.1], outside the ten supplied bodies. The supporting BJ1805.11160v1 Theorem4.13 has standing smooth-projective scope, and its Lemma4.15 proof invokes an external lattice saturation lemma. No independently justified extension of that approximation argument to these singular quotients is supplied. The finite Rees-module argument in n1 compares Veroneses of one finite-type norm; it cannot replace approximation of an arbitrary obstacle norm by growing finite-type norms. This gap is not evidence that the obstacle equality is false.

BJ Theorem8.5/Corollary8.6, LF4843--4862, really differentiate E-downarrow on every projective E1 potential without an envelope hypothesis; the additional equality with E(P(.)) retains that hypothesis. Thus an unproved singular envelope theorem is not made an artificial prerequisite here. The actual missing prerequisite is the obstacle-volume approximation.

If the bounded estimate were proved for cone F, n2's Reeb continuity and n1's actual bounded MA convergence would pass it to irrational fields; decreasing outer continuity and the existing genuine same-Reeb mixed-MA continuity would then pass it to E1. For continuous f approximated by f_m in D, Lipschitzness and probability mass give the remainder-quotient bound 2||f-f_m||+C_(Q,f_m)|t|, with m chosen before t. This is a transfer implication here, not an established cone derivative, and gives no quadratic estimate for every continuous direction or uniformity over its unit ball.

Details and source corrections are in P13.1-argument.md Sections10--14 and source-extracts/source-provenance.json. Uniform differentiation of actual cone energy remains unresolved.

notes.text:
